title: D, E and F regions
idea: D is lowest and soaks up low bands by day. E bends signals back for hops up to 1,200 miles; F2, the highest, up to 2,500.

rows: By day, absorbs signals below about 10 MHz. Gone at night.
Short range at high angles, from a low dipole

compare.how: D layer present: low bands absorbed for long distance. F splits into F1 and F2.
D layer gone: 160, 80 and 40 meters go long distance.
Short-distance MF or HF at high elevation angles.

traps.why: One F2 hop is about 2,500 miles. Farther needs more hops.
That's F2. The lower E region hops about 1,200 miles.
It's about height: the highest layer gives the longest hop.

traps.wrong: The F region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours
traps.why: It's the D region that absorbs the low bands by day.
NVIS is short-distance propagation at high elevation angles.

traps.wrong: A horizontal dipole placed at approximately 1/2 wavelength above the ground
traps.why: Half a wavelength up sends energy at lower angles. For NVIS, mount it low: 1/10 to 1/4 wavelength.
